text:
alex: Captured a 30s nsys trace of a heavy q8 batch run — seeing weird gaps where memcpy seems to block kernels on stream 3. Upload: https://internal-artifacts/trace/2149997777.nsight :thinking_face:

maria: link looks good. which model/config?

alex: gpt-medium-quant q8, sequence 1024, batcher=continuous, kvcache enabled, prefetch=on, kernel selection heuristic = 'latency-optimized'

chen: can you paste the nsys summary waterfall snippet? Also did you sample with CPU pinned threads?

alex: paste of the waterfall timeline region (abridged):
```
# nsight waterfall
[0.000s] h2d memcpy (stream 2) 0.8ms
[0.001s] kernel GEMM (stream 0) 4.2ms
[0.005s] async prefetch memcpy (stream 3) 1.3ms -> blocks kernel on stream 0 at 0.006s
[0.007s] kernel ATTENTION (stream 0) 6.1ms (queued)
[0.015s] CPU scheduling lull ~25ms (thread sleep -> prefetch delayed)
[0.040s] host-to-device large memcpy (stream 3) 10ms overlaps with stream 0 kernels causing serialization
```

alex: the surprising bit is the host memcpy on stream 3 seems to serialize kernels on stream 0 even though they should run concurrently.

sam: ninja question: is stream 3 using blocking cudaMemcpy (synchronous) or async `cudaMemcpyAsync`?

alex: async, pinned pool enabled. But trace shows host thread performing copies in bursts and then CPU gets preempted.

devon: I saw similar before — CPU preemption of the thread that issues async copies can delay submission of kernels and create apparent memcpy->kernel blocking. Check if the submission thread got migrated.

chen: two quick checks: 1) were copies using `cudaMemcpyAsync(..., stream)` with host memory pinned? 2) what's the libcu pointer for prefetcher thread?

alex: yes pinned. command used: `python -m runner --prefetcher=parallel --fill_pinned_pool=true --batcher=continuous`

infra-bot: perf center notice: host cpu 0-2 saturated during trace window; cgroup throttling: none.

maria: try switching prefetcher to 'submit-only' mode (issue all memcpys from a dedicated pinned thread pinned to a core) and re-run capture. That isolates scheduler noise.

sam: also try forcing stream priorities: set kernel stream high priority, prefetch stream low. If overlap improves it's a submission timing problem rather than CUDA engine contention.

alex: did a short run toggling stream priorities: low-priority memcpy (stream 3) + high-priority kernel (stream 0) yielded better overlap but still occasional 20-30ms stalls.

chen: post the kernel selection log — maybe the runtime is swapping to a fallback kernel when sequence length changes and that kernel is single-streamed.

alex: log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-17 14:23:12] kernel_selector: selected kernel attention_fp16_sm80_optimized
[2026-03-17 14:23:14] fallback: attention_generic_small_seqlen activated (reason: cache-miss on tiled params)
```

alex: the fallback corresponds to the big host memcpy earlier. Might be a param upload path causing pinned pool refill.

devon: aha — if tiled weights are being uploaded lazily on fallback, that triggers large host->device memcpys on the prefetch stream which bursts and blocks submission. We should ensure model params are resident before serving or pre-warm tiled kernels.

maria: for immediate triage: 1) run trace with `--preload-weights` to avoid lazy uploads; 2) set prefetcher to dedicate a pinned thread with CPU affinity; 3) compare with `--batcher=microbatch` to see if batching heuristic exacerbates the serialization.

alex: I'll run three quick captures tonight and post diffs. One more data point: perf counters show host copy throughput ~8GB/s sustained during stalls — suggests many large transfers.

sam: q: could quantized kernels trigger extra unpacking host-side? Some q8 paths unpack blocks on CPU and upload unpacked tiles.

chen: yes that's possible — check the quantization unpack path. If unpacking is on the submission thread, it will cause CPU jitter and delayed CUDA calls. Move unpack to a background worker.

alex: noted. Also seeing a mild perf regression after kernel selection change last week (rollout id: r-2026-03-10). May roll back selector to previous version for A/B to confirm.

devon: for long-term: add telemetry for "bytes uploaded during request" and mark whether upload happened during inference vs preloaded. That will make these cases visible in dashboards.

maria: agreed. Also add an nsight capture guide to devex: how to correlate CPU scheduling gaps with CUDA submission times — we've lost this signal often in tickets.

alex: thanks team. I'll attach the three traces once complete and open a short RFC for pre-warming heuristics.

infra-bot: trace upload complete: https://internal-artifacts/trace/2149997777_variants.zip :thumbsup:

sam: ping me after uploads, I can run a quick kernel timeline diff tool I have.

alex: will do. Closing for now — will follow up with diffs. :sparkles:
